expectations.text: A1 Zones marked and ordered: the document opens with a human zone whose heading or banner names its audience (a pointer line in the header does not count), and any AI-input or archive material sits last in its own labelled zone; nothing for people follows machine content

Archive-type material does sit last (Appendix A line 204, Appendix B line 235) but is not in a labelled zone: the headings are 'Appendix A. Evidence and method' and 'Appendix B. Q3 2026 incident summary', and neither names a bin (archive / AI input).

Appendix A (file table, A.2, A.3 data notes) and Appendix B (two aggregate tables, lines 235-264) are open on the page, and neither opens with a line naming its bin or what it supports. expectations.text: B1 Reading path: within 60 lines of the title there are at least 3 links to sections, each saying what the reader gets, and a line saying who can stop where

expectations.text: B2 Order follows understanding: the mental model comes first, terms are defined before the first section that uses them, and chronology lives in the archive

'Option C' is introduced on line 11; 'which both B and C need' (line 24) and 'fall back to Option B' (line 28) are used before the options table (header line 35) defines A/B/C. expectations.text: B3 The H2 headings of the human zone, read alone, give the outline or the argument; question and decision headings carry their answer or ask
expectations.evidence: H2s are '1. Recommendation', '2. Options', '3. Evidence', '4. Plan', '5. Risks', '6. Open questions and assumptions', '7. Decision record', 'Appendix A. Evidence and method', 'Appendix B. Q3 2026 incident summary'. Read alone they are generic topic labels, not the argument: 'Recommendation' does not carry the recommendation, and 'Open questions and assumptions' and 'Decision record' carry no answer or ask. Only an H3 (3.1 'The risk is concentrated in two services') is argumentative.

expectations.text: C1 Conclusion first: the glance panel opens the document straight after the title and one metadata line, and its bottom line states the conclusion itself, not what the document covers

Directly after the H1 come five metadata, provenance and reading-guide bullets (lines 3-7: For, Decision needed by, Prepared, Based on, Reading guide), not one metadata line, and there is no separate glance panel; provenance and a reading guide sit ahead of the conclusion. The conclusion itself is stated plainly once Section 1 starts (line 11: 'Split the upgrade (Option C). Move the seven services that passed staging to v10 before the code freeze...'), so only the position and format fail.

expectations.text: C2 Compact panel: about 300 words of prose or fewer (tables and picture excluded; mechanical.json gives panel_words), one line per decision and per risk, and verdict, decisions and top risks fit the first screen
expectations.evidence: mechanical.json panel_words=495 against a budget of about 300 (check_doc C2: 'the first section runs to about 495 words'). Section 1 (lines 9-31) is a recommendation paragraph, five 'Why' items, four numbered decisions (several run 2-3 sentences, e.g. line 24) and two multi-sentence gate bullets, so decisions are not one line each. No risk lines appear in the first screen at all; the risk table is in Section 5 (line 144).

expectations.text: C3 Verdict, decisions and risks are complete and loud in the panel: the verdict has a glyph, confidence and basis; each decision has who, what, by when and a recommendation; at most 5 ranked risks, each with severity and consequence

Decisions (lines 21-26) give what and by-when ('Decisions needed by Friday 2026-10-23'; 'ordered by Thursday 2026-11-05') but no per-decision owner (Marcus appears only in the header) and the recommendation is implicit in 'Approve...'. Risks: none in the opening section; the Section 5 table (lines 144-153) lists R1-R6 as 'Risk | Why it matters | Response' with no severity and no ranking.

expectations.text: C4 Nothing invented: no verdict, decision or risk block without grounding in the sources, any ranking is traceable, empty slots are omitted
expectations.evidence: Checked verdict, decisions and risks against the inputs; each is grounded. Verdict: 7 of 9 pass staging, auth-service fails 2 of 148, user-store untested, no rollback for the two (upgrade-notes.md, services.csv). Decisions: $18,000 ordered by 2026-11-05, Data team Monday start and the CAB exception rule are all in upgrade-notes.md. Risks R1-R6 are built from gaps in the notes and say so ('the notes do not say staging ran this mix'; R4 'This is an inference, not a finding'). Author additions are labelled: key dates 'Derived, proposed' / 'Proposed' (lines 98, 103) and assumptions in 6.2. No ranking is claimed for R1-R6. No panel slot is padded; the blank Section 7 decision record (line 182) is a deliberate form for Marcus's outcome (the audit-trail ask), not template filler. Close call on the blank record.

expectations.text: C5 Numbers in the panel trace to the sources (spot-check at least three); derived, merged or de-duplicated numbers say so
expectations.evidence: Section 1 numbers checked: '2 of 148 integration tests' and 'estimated at 4 hours' (upgrade-notes.md); '$18,000 ... ordered by Thursday 2026-11-05 to be active on 2026-11-12' (notes; 5 Nov 2026 is a Thursday); Identity engineer on leave 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-13 (notes); 'called directly by 6 of the other 8 services, and 7 of the 8 depend on user-store' (services.csv: 6 callers, 7 via transitive closure); 'five failed rollouts (all SEV3) ... 10-19 minutes' (incidents-q3.csv: 10, 14, 15, 15, 19); 'about three times the longest incident (78 minutes)' (240/78 = 3.08). uncertainties: Extended-support terms: assumed a flat $18,000 with a 3-month term from 2026-11-12; this decides whether Option C is cheaper than B and whether January needs $18,000 or $36,000.
Freeze rules: assumed 'P1' means SEV1-class and flagged whether a rollback is exempt for CAB.
Which auth-service version the seven staging passes ran against; if it was v10 with the shim, a re-run on v8 is needed (Gate 1, described as the biggest hole).
Capacity: only the Data team's capacity is stated; Platform and Integration slots and whether 'one week' includes production rollout are unknown.
Data currency: the inventory and the incident log carry no as-of date (log ends 2026-09-28); staging results of 2026-10-09 to 10-11 assumed to still hold.
Approximate figures: the 41% share and the 'about two incidents' estimate use rows as logged and a 92-day quarter; they show scale only.
Rendering was checked with a local CommonMark engine, not in the repo host; the checksum check can fail after a git line-ending conversion.
needs_review: Confirm the three assumptions listed in the final reply: flat $18,000 for a 3-month term, 'P1' = SEV1-class, and the wave dates and 2026-12-15 checkpoint, which are the executor's proposals.

The reading of depends_on as 'caller depends on callee', the pairing of auth-service and user-store, the two gates and the slow-dependency check before gateway are the executor's proposals, not the teams' positions.
The decision record and evidence structure were added because of the audit-trail request and are easy to drop; there is no author line (git history carries it).
workarounds: None; no skill was used. Chose plain Markdown with a PNG figure and Graphviz source so the report renders in VS Code, GitHub and Azure DevOps without Mermaid.

suggestions.assertion: Key risks present: the 12 Nov end of support and the missing rollback path for auth-service (and user-store) appear among the top risks
suggestions.reason: 'Among the top risks' is ambiguous when a document has no risk panel. Here the rollback gap is in the opening 'Why' list but not in the Section 5 risk table, and the 12 Nov end of support is the reverse. Say where to look (for example the risk lines within the first 60 lines) so graders rule the same way.

suggestions.assertion: D5 D6 Explained and reproducible: alt text, a caption saying how to read the diagram and its takeaway, a legend ...
suggestions.reason: Six sub-requirements sit in one boolean. This run has alt text, an in-image legend, the relation stated, a .dot beside the PNG and an edge-list CSV, and fails only because the caption is a provenance line. Splitting 'explained' (alt, caption, legend, relation) from 'reproducible' (source file, archive edge list) would show which half failed.

suggestions.assertion: E1 E2 Honesty: every judgment has a confidence level and its basis; content not in the inputs ... is labelled as such; unknowns are listed
suggestions.reason: Two rules in one boolean hide a lopsided result: this run fully passes E2 (inferences labelled, assumptions and unknowns listed) and fully fails E1 (no confidence level anywhere). Split them.

suggestions.assertion: C4 Nothing invented: ... empty slots are omitted
suggestions.reason: 'Empty slots are omitted' collides with a deliberately blank decision-record table (this run's Section 7), which an audit-trail request arguably invites. State whether the clause applies only to the glance panel.

suggestions.assertion: D2 Coverage and truth: ... inferred edges are dashed and captioned
suggestions.reason: The clause is satisfied vacuously when no inferred edge is drawn, and the assertion does not say how to treat an aggregate arrow (here one 'cluster -> auth-service, 6 services' arrow standing for six edges). Add that an aggregate arrow is fine when every member edge exists in services.csv.

suggestions.assertion: F3 Chat reply: ... the file path, where to start ...
suggestions.reason: 'Where to start' is hard to judge when the reply just lists several files. Require an explicit pointer such as 'start at Section 1', and say whether naming the decision plus its deadline is required (this reply omits the Friday 23 Oct deadline entirely).

eval_feedback.overall: The structural assertions (A, B, C1-C3, automatic checks) separate this answer-first but unzoned report from a skill-shaped one clearly, and the content assertions (Figures, Audit data kept, Verdict and ask) check specific values rather than mere presence. Weak spots are the bundled D5 D6 and E1 E2 booleans and a few scope ambiguities (top risks, empty slots, aggregate edges). No assertion checks the correctness of the other body numbers; I verified them all and found no errors.
